hints.junior: The null check wasn't dead code — it was the only thing handling the still-loading state. The AI just never saw that caller.
hints.mid: Nothing threw. The function still returned a string on every call — just the wrong one for one specific input the AI's context window didn't include.
hints.staff: This isn't a model-quality problem. Diff review exists to catch exactly this class of miss: a locally-reasonable edit that's wrong for a reason outside the edited function.

hints.junior: Click Reject in diff-review mode — the test call underneath still shows the correct output, because nothing merged.
hints.mid: Same proposed edit in both modes. Only whether it applies immediately vs. waits on your explicit decision changes.
hints.staff: The live test call re-invokes whatever the current function body actually is right now — it's not a canned before/after, the runtime output really does flip on Accept.

hints.junior: Diff review isn't about not trusting AI — it's the same review step you'd want on a teammate's PR, just pointed at a different author.
hints.mid: GitHub Copilot's own review surface renders suggestions as diffs with per-suggestion Accept/Dismiss — this pattern isn't hypothetical, it's what the real tool does.
hints.staff: The required decision point is what does the work. A diff you can scroll past without deciding anything gives you the appearance of review with none of the protection.

hints.junior: Put Reject as close to Accept as Accept is to itself — a UI that buries rejection nudges people toward rubber-stamping.
hints.mid: Log who accepted or rejected each suggestion, not just who committed — git blame alone can't answer whether a diff was actually read.
hints.staff: aria-live announcing the applied/rejected result matters here specifically — a screen reader user has no equivalent of "watching the code visibly change" without it.

sections.junior: Here's a real failure mode with AI code suggestions: one gets applied straight to your file, no diff, no confirmation, and a defensive check just quietly disappears.
sections.mid: This case is about a null check that got auto-removed by an AI suggestion, and showed up three days later as NaN prices in production.
sections.staff: We're covering why diff review, not model quality, is the actual safeguard against context the AI never had visibility into.

sections.junior: The fix is simple: show the change, and make the person click Accept or Reject before anything merges.
sections.mid: This mirrors how you'd review a teammate's pull request, just applied to an AI-authored change instead.
sections.staff: The protection comes from the required decision blocking the merge, not from rendering a diff someone can passively scroll past.

sections.junior: Try both modes here. In auto-apply, the fix lands the second you click the button. In diff review, it waits for you to say yes.
sections.mid: Watch the test call underneath — it's live, so you'll see the real output change the moment the edit actually takes effect.
sections.staff: Reject in diff-review mode and confirm the test call still returns the original, correct output — nothing touched the function.

sections.junior: A diff makes a removed check obvious. A finished file doesn't. That difference is the whole point of this pattern.
sections.mid: Route AI suggestions through a real diff-and-decide step, the same one you'd want for any other author's change.
sections.staff: Required decision beats passive diff every time — build the review step so it can't be skimmed past.
